Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Gameplay 2.1 Turns 2.2 Objectives 2.3 Plots and Irrigation 3 Growing Bamboo 4 Improvements 5 Completing Objectives and game end 6 Variants 6.1 Rule Differences Between First and Second Edition Overview The Japanese Emperor has been given a fantastic gift--a Chinese Giant Panda! But all this thing does is tear up the garden and eat bamboo. To keep the emperor's garden pristine, you'll have to direct the gardener, irrigate the plots, and lure the panda into eating the right bamboo shoots. And then there's the weather to deal with. The player who manages the garden best wins! Gameplay Everything starts with the garden's central pond. The gardener and panda are sitting here, waiting for you to expand the area. Each player takes turns adding plots to the garden, moving the gardener and panda around, and irrigating plots. This is all to fulfill objectives, which earn you points. The first player to complete nine objectives invokes the end of the game. At that point, every other player gets one more turn. The points for each player's completed objectives are summed up. The one with the most is the winner. Turns Each turn consists of 2 steps: Weather First, the weather die is rolled (except in the player's first turn) to determine that turn's weather. Weather has random effects at the start of the player's turn. Those effects are: Weather Symbol Description Sun Take a third action Rain Grow 1 bamboo on any irrigated plot Wind May take two identical actions this turn Storm Move panda to any plot where it eats a bamboo as normal Clouds Add an improvement to a plot without one. If no improvements are available, you may choose another type of weather. Question Mark -- Choose any weather type Fulfilling the weather effects is always optional. Actions After weather is determined, the player takes two actions. They cannot be the same action (unless the weather is "wind"). Available Actions Name Symbol Description Plots Draw 3 plot tiles. Choose one to place adjacent to the pond or 2 other existing plots. (There are 26 plots in total.) Irrigation Place an irrigation channel between two garden plots. Gardener Move the gardener any number of tiles in a straight line. Bamboo will grow on it and any adjacent irrigated tiles of the same color. Panda Move the panda any number of tiles in a straight line. The panda eats one section of bamboo, which gets added to your reserve. Objective Take an objective card from one of the three categories (plot, panda, gardener). If the objective is already reflected in the garden's current state, it is discarded. You may choose another objective. (This is the only situation where an action can be cancelled and a different action can be taken.) Objectives A player may claim completed objectives any time during their turn. There are three kinds: Plot : Fulfilled if there is a plot configuration as shown (color and shape). All plots must be irrigated. Panda : Fulfilled if you have bamboo units of the matching color. These are returned to the reserve after the objective is completed. Gardener : Fulfilled if the gardener is on any plot with the matching improvements and bamboo of the given height. You can have no more than five objective cards at a time. If completing a gardener objective, the gardener must be on the plot (or one of the plots) that fulfills the objective. A long time ago at the Japanese Imperial court, the Chinese Emperor offered a giant panda bear as a symbol of peace to the Japanese Emperor. Since then, the Japanese Emperor has entrusted his court members (the players) with the difficult task of caring for the animal by tending to his bamboo garden.

In Takenoko, the players will cultivate land plots, irrigate them, and grow one of the three species of bamboo (Green, Yellow, and Pink) with the help of the Imperial gardener to maintain this bamboo garden. They will have to bear with the immoderate hunger of this sacred animal for the juicy and tender bamboo. The player who manages his land plots best, growing the most bamboo while feeding the delicate appetite of the panda, will win the game.

[Rating: 1/10] Better than Tokaido. Not sure if that's saying much. Certainly I see a design approach: let's put scores on cards and cards tell you what you do. Seems a bit lazy: here there actions you can do, and here are cards which reward these actions. I don't see anything that would tie the game together, on the mechanical level at least. It's just pieces put together in the same box.   While the game is an enjoyable family type fare, there's really no rhyme or reason to it's theme. Who are we? What are we doing? What's this panda doing in the garden? The booklet explains it, with this far fetched tale 

[Rating: 1/10] My wife and I played this with another couple. The couple got this for the holidays and were eager to try it out. The couples 3 year old would pop up every 10 min. wanting to see what was going on and I'd play with him for a bit until it was my turn. By the end I was so board I would just do my turn as quickly as possible and then go watch The Incredibles with the 3 year old in the other room. Towards the end of the game one of the adults came in and told me I won.  I was never invested in the game and I never tried to interact with the other players. Somehow I won without even trying. [Rating: 1/10] Was super excited to play this with my family but I can't because the designers didn't consider red/green color blind players. Super frustrating. I'm a game developer and it should be common designer knowledge that around 10% of men are red/green color blind. :( (sold on eBay for $15 2021)

[Rating: 1/10] Not color blind friendly (even though it would be very easy to add symbols to colors). In fact, it is enemy of color blind people (you shouldn't even try to play). Also, the goal cards have confusing rules for first time players (on the X that define some aditional rules to complete goals).

[Rating: 1/10] I bounced off of this game because certain outcomes on the weather die rolls seemed far too influential on the game.

[Rating: 1/10] :star::nostar::nostar::nostar::nostar:  Update: I am done with this game.  It's alright. The game is telling you how to play the game. But the shared board is interesting in a decent way, but has risk of being arbitrary - so strong that the game can decide who wins and who loses

[Rating: 1/10] Looks gorgeous, great theme but it is random nonsense as there is something off with the objectives (dice/random draw/unbalanced objectives). It's also too long for what it is. Girls grew bored as it was Panda, Panda, Panda eat that bamboo!

[Rating: 1/10] FLGS said my girls ages 8-10 would like this.  They did not like it much.  To much down time.  Broken read BGG to fix it.  Multi-player solitaire. Played 10 times.

[Rating: 2/10] The production is impressive. This is a pretty game. The gameplay: not so much. The cards are totally out of balance. Cards that vary wildly in completion difficulty score similar points. And the endgame is plagued by the luck of drawing cards where the conditions have already been met, or require 1 simple action. Also the luck of having other people either complete or contribute to your missions is overwhelming. A terrible design.
